claims.claim: Born in New York; based in Atlanta, Georgia
claims.note: Legit.ng gives New York as birthplace and Atlanta, Georgia as current residence.

claims.claim: Mafiathon is a month-long subathon streamed around the clock
claims.note: TechTimes: streamed 24 hours a day for the entire month.

claims.claim: Mafiathon 2 ran through November 2024, 24 hours a day, starting in early November
claims.note: TechTimes: kicked off in early November 2024, 24 hours a day for the month. The end date is no longer stated.

claims.claim: Mafiathon 2 total 728,532 subscribers, more than doubling Ironmouse

claims.claim: TechTimes gives 727,700 in its article body

claims.claim: Record fell on day 24 when he passed 728,600 subscribers

claims.note: Tribune: broke the Twitch subscriber world record for the third time during Mafiathon 3.

claims.claim: Mafiathon 3 was his third and final Mafiathon
claims.note: Dexerto: 'Kai Cenat's third and final Mafiathon'.

claims.claim: Streams Charts counted 1,112,947 subscriptions by the end of Mafiathon 3
claims.note: Dexerto (Streams Charts data): 1,112,947 subscriptions.

claims.claim: 85.23 million hours watched; Dexerto's headline says more viewers than 2025's top subathons combined

claims.claim: Cenat was Twitch's most-watched American streamer of 2025 with 134.4 million hours, nearly double Asmongold
claims.note: Streams Charts data via Dexerto: 134.4M hours, Asmongold second with 76.53M.

claims.claim: In 2025 TIME named him to its inaugural TIME100 Creators list

claims.claim: That year he hosted Streamer University at the University of Akron in Ohio
claims.note: Tubefilter: first Streamer University on the University of Akron campus.

claims.claim: Event featured more than 150 creators and 27 million hours of watch time
claims.note: Tubefilter: more than 150 creators and 27 million hours of watch time.

claims.claim: Cenat hosts the school as headmaster
claims.note: Tubefilter: Cenat served as headmaster.

claims.claim: Dexerto wrote that he had taken over the headlines, most famously with Streamer University
claims.note: Dexerto's own wording: 'Kai has taken over headlines throughout the last year, most famously holding his viral Streamer University'.

claims.claim: Quote: 'As a streamer, you're not in a box. You're not trapped'
claims.note: Dexerto quotes Cenat telling TIME the line.

claims.claim: Tubefilter described his Twitch account as dormant

claims.note: Tubefilter (Vivet) and AY Magazine (Arkansas event) support both parts.

claims.note: Tubefilter: 23-minute vlog on a 'secret third account', titled 'I Quit'.

claims.claim: Tubefilter reported he is not quitting streaming; the title refers to personal goals
claims.note: Tubefilter headline and text confirm.

claims.claim: He said he was having 'a lot of self-doubt' about stepping back from content creation
claims.note: Tubefilter quotes 'having a lot of self-doubt'.

claims.claim: Vivet's name comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to live'
claims.note: Tubefilter: name from a Latin verb meaning 'to live'.

claims.claim: Three months in Italy with tailors; consulted American designers in Atlanta
claims.note: Tubefilter confirms both.

claims.claim: Tubefilter presents Vivet as one of several ambitious projects alongside Mafiathons and Streamer University
claims.note: Tubefilter: one of several ambitious projects, citing Mafiathons and Streamer University as evidence of follow-through.

claims.claim: In early June 2026 Cenat confirmed the sequel; teaser drew 2.5 million Instagram likes in under two days
claims.note: Tubefilter (9 June 2026): 2.5M Instagram likes in less than two days.

claims.claim: Creators could apply through the official site; selected alumni would return
claims.note: Tubefilter confirms both.

claims.claim: By mid-July the event was at Hendrix College in Conway, Arkansas; Cenat on site; 100+ channels live at all times

claims.claim: Cenat announced a giveaway of video game consoles and electronics in Union Square, Manhattan; thousands gathered
claims.note: NY1: giveaway of consoles and electronics luring thousands of fans to Union Square. No date given, and the body now gives none.

claims.claim: The crowd caused damage and scores of people were arrested
claims.note: NY1: scores arrested, damage to cars, buses and storefronts.

claims.claim: Cenat was charged with inciting a riot and promoting an unlawful gathering
claims.note: NY1 confirms both charges.

claims.claim: In his apology he referred to 'the disruption and damage to the community, the park, the vehicles, and the storefronts in the area'
claims.note: Quote confirmed.

claims.claim: In May 2024 prosecutors said they would drop the charges after Cenat apologized for the disruption and damage
claims.note: NY1: charges dropped after apology and restitution. No Snapchat reference remains.

claims.claim: Cenat and two co-defendants agreed to pay over $57,000; Cenat's $55,000 went to Union Square Partnership for cleanup and landscaping
claims.note: NY1: more than $57,000 in total; $55,000 from Cenat to the Union Square Partnership for cleanup and landscaping repairs.

valueNote: Clear timeline built on several outlets, with sources that disagree now flagged or avoided. Residual note: the metaDescription and section context still refer to the 2023 Union Square case; the NY1 extract did not state the year, but the riot's 2023 date is consistent with the source's framing.
summary: Approved on second pass. All corrections from the first pass are applied: the Mafiathon 2 end date is removed, the superlative is replaced with the Dexerto headline wording, TIME's line is attributed to Dexerto, the TIME list is dated 2025, the YourRAGE and dormant wording matches Tubefilter, the Vivet paraphrase and Snapchat detail are removed, and the 4 August date is removed.
